name: Pollution
description: Smog you can see: it rises, gathers over your base and poisons what is under it.

pages.title: Pollution
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() Burning and crushing make **smog you can see**: grey carbon, yellow sulfur and dust
- It rises and gathers in a cloud high over your base
- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() A thick cloud poisons everything under it
- Wind moves it slowly, so a factory needs **exhaust and filters**

Smog is real gas: blocks you can see and walk through. Fresh smoke rises until a roof or the cloud layer stops it (Y191, sulfur Y190) and settles there.\
\
Under a roof it fills the room from the top down. Out in the open it gathers over the [#](7A3C9A)[chunk](entry://glossary/chunk)[#]() that made it.

pages.title: Seeing smog
pages.text: Look at a gas block to see what it is and how thick it is (light, medium or heavy: 1 to 3 units). Crouch to look through it at the block behind.

pages.title: What pollutes
pages.text:
- Furnace, smoker, blast furnace: 1 carbon and 0.1 sulfur per coal burned; other fuels have their own amounts
- Blaze Burner, steam boiler, Farmer's Delight stove: about 1 carbon a minute while fuelled
- Campfire: a little now and then
- Crushing Wheels: about 4 dust a minute while working, Millstone 1

pages.title: Bulk smelting
pages.text: An [#](2E5AAC)[Encased Fan](entry://create_basics/fans)[#]() blowing through lava or a Blaze Burner makes no smog by itself. Each item it finishes puffs out smog right where it is: 1 carbon for every item blasted, plus 1 sulfur for every 5, and 1 carbon for every item smoked over fire or a campfire. A stack of 64 ores makes 64 carbon. Washing and haunting are clean.

pages.title: Engines
pages.text: [#](2E5AAC)[TFMG](entry://industry/tfmg_engines)[#]() engines, coke ovens and blast furnaces pollute for the fuel they burn, so idle ones are clean.

pages.title: The cloud
pages.text:
A chunk's pollution is the gas in the cloud layer above it. A gas block holds 1 to 3 units (light, medium, heavy).\
\
Carbon is measured against 512 units a chunk, sulfur against 128. The effects below start at a share of that.

pages.title: What it does
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** under a carbon cloud:
- 30%% Mining Fatigue
- 40%% Hunger
- 50%% Weakness
- 60%% Slowness
- 70%% Poison
- 80%% Nausea
- 90%% Wither

Under a sulfur cloud:
- 30%% Blindness
- 60%% Poison
- 90%% Wither

Standing inside gas blinds you, and sulfur also poisons you. A respirator keeps it out.

pages.title: Acid rain
pages.text:
Sulfur in the air and in the rain kills crops, berry bushes, sugar cane, bamboo, ferns and bee nests. It turns grass, moss and farmland to podzol and pollutes water.\
\
Carbon in rain makes grass and plants grow. Stone and anything you build are never harmed.

pages.title: Wind
pages.text: Wind pushes smog sideways a few blocks at a time, so a small base's smoke drifts off. Smog never fades on its own: a factory's cloud keeps growing until its exhaust is filtered.

pages.title: Aerometer
pages.text: Its needle shows how much smog is around you, and it beeps near gas. Put it in an item frame as an alarm.

pages.title: Explosions
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** a machine whose smoke has nowhere to go, such as a sealed room already full of gas, blows up after a few tries and breaks. See [#](2E5AAC)[Pressure and Sealed Casings](entry://survival/smog_pressure)[#]().\
\
Fire, torches and lava never set smog off.
